target_surface: The fixed-work exponentiation forms an all-zero/all-one 32-bit selector mask directly from each secret-derived exponent bit.

primary_masking_literature.title: On the Cost of Lazy Engineering for Masked Software Implementations
primary_masking_literature.relevance: Defines value- versus transition-based leakage and experimentally shows why careless assembly/share reuse can reduce masking order.
primary_masking_literature.not_a_drop_in: It supplies a leakage-model and engineering warning, not a masked SQIsign or modular-exponentiation implementation.

primary_masking_literature.title: Threshold Implementations in Software: Micro-architectural Leakages in Algorithms
primary_masking_literature.relevance: Derives share-placement conditions for scalar processors and validates transition/glitch-aware implementations on RISC-V and ARM Cortex-M4.
primary_masking_literature.not_a_drop_in: Its PRESENT/Keccak constructions do not supply masked big-integer Montgomery arithmetic for SQIsign.

primary_masking_literature.title: Efficient Second-Order Masked Software Implementations of Ascon in Theory and Practice
primary_masking_literature.relevance: Uses share rotations and final-assembly/netlist plus physical validation to harden masked software against unintended share combination.
primary_masking_literature.not_a_drop_in: The optimized Ascon/Keccak gadgets are algorithm-specific and do not establish security for SQIsign arithmetic.

candidate.shares: choose uniform S; share0=S and share1=S XOR M
candidate.attraction: each individual share and its static Hamming weight have the same marginal distribution for b=0 and b=1

leakage_models.static_hamming_weight: Observe one share value or its Hamming weight in isolation.
leakage_models.sequential_hamming_distance: Observe the data/register-bus transition share0 -> share1 when both shares are processed serially on one core.
leakage_models.scope_warning: The HD result is an architectural software-masking hazard, not proof that a particular compiler places both shares in one register or that an external probe resolves the transition.

full_word_symbolic_result.recombined_mask: share0 XOR share1 = 0x00000000 for b=0 and 0xffffffff for b=1

required_next_design: Use a reviewed software masking gadget and composable leakage model for the selector and arithmetic state, not only secret-independent share marginals.
Account for register reuse, bus transitions, glitches, compiler spills, share ordering and randomness refresh on Cortex-M33.
Keep shares separated in source and final assembly and test transition-aware first-/higher-order leakage physically.
Mask or hide the exponent-prefix-dependent Montgomery state as well as the selector bit; selector-only masking cannot close the published attack surface.
claim_boundary: This artifact is an exact abstract HW/HD check for a naive selector-share representation. It is not a masked Montgomery implementation, compiler proof, probing-security proof, physical measurement, or claim that every two-share gadget fails.
